title: Canonical comparison of normalized and embedding finite-field scalar extension
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, a Noetherian finite-dimensional scheme $T$ on which $\ell$ is invertible, and finite coefficient fields $E\subset F$ in $\Omega$. Use the canonical small coefficient models and completed coefficient maps of [def-weil-pbc-finite-completed-coefficient-map]. Let $Q_E$ denote the integral localization, and $S_{E,F}$ the normalized finite-stage transition of [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category]. Let $S^{\rm raw}_{E,F}$ be the embedding scalar extension of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], evaluated on these same small fields and their transported inclusion. Define $c_{E,F}:S_{E,F}\xrightarrow\sim S^{\rm raw}_{E,F}$ as the unique natural isomorphism whose component on every integral object $Q_E(K)$ is the specified integral/rational scalar comparison of [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category], under the canonical equality of the actual completed coefficient maps and hence the integral tensor objects. The equality is fixed by all finite quotient projections, which are the same transported field inclusion. At $E=F$ this comparison is precisely the specified tensor-multiplication unit. This defines a comparison of the two existing scalar constructions, without choosing a new coefficient map or discarding the reflexive case.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2), Remark 6.8.15; Stacks 03EK and 0D6D. Canonical identity of the two quotient-normalized coefficient maps and integral scalar constructions used in the rational realization comparison.

proof.text: For each finite quotient, the two integer inclusions and their induced quotient ring maps are definitionally identical. The constant-section normalization of pbcLevelConstantComparison in [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-tower] identifies its hom with sheafification of the constants-to-functions map. Naturality of that map under the quotient inclusion shows that pbcFiniteScalarMap equals the finite coefficientMap used by pbcScalarCoefficientMap in [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. The uniqueness clause of [def-weil-pbc-finite-completed-coefficient-map], tested on every finite projection, now identifies the completed maps.
proof.elementary: Equality of quotient lifts, naturality of sheafification, and application of the existing uniqueness theorem.

proof.text: Apply the same derived extension functor to the equal completed coefficient maps. The integral restrictions from [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category] and [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] are lifts of this same functor to the same full subcategory; their membership proofs agree by proof irrelevance. The embedding scalar localization formula at scalar 1 gives an equality of functors: integral tensor followed by target localization equals source localization followed by raw embedding tensor.
proof.elementary: Congruence, proof irrelevance, functor extensionality, and specialization of pbcScalarLocalization_naturality.

proof.text: Use the existing pbcScalarIntegralComparison of [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category]. After transporting by the functor equality of Step 2, its components define the required isomorphism on every object of raw localization [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization]. To check naturality for a localized arrow f, clear its denominator: s*f=Q(u) for a power s of the uniformizer, by Mathlib IsLocalizedModule.surj for base change. Q(s*id) is invertible, with inverse the reciprocal scalar times the identity. Precompose the desired equation by its image and use integral naturality for u and s*id; cancellation proves the equation. NatIso.ofComponents therefore supplies the comparison. The argument does not distinguish equal from distinct fields, so at equal fields it retains exactly the prescribed tensor-multiplication unit.
proof.elementary: The fraction calculation is proved explicitly in rawScalar_naturality using Mathlib localization surjectivity and units, tensor balancing, functoriality, and cancellation of an invertible arrow.

proof.text: Every raw localized object is literally the localization of its underlying integral object [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization]. The required HEq therefore fixes every hom component. Natural-transformation extensionality, followed by isomorphism extensionality, proves uniqueness. The existing definition chooses this unique normalized comparison.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2), Remark 6.8.15; explicit identification and scalar-localization descent of the existing constructions, preserving their integral normalization.
